title: Restore t2fanrd fan control after suspend/resume on T2 Macs
author: vivekchauhan
body:
Fixes #12393.

## Problem
t2fanrd holds applesmc fan FDs open across suspend. After resume the sysfs nodes are recreated and the running daemon never reasserts manual control, leaving the SMC in failsafe full speed: fan1_manual=0 with the fan stuck at max while temperatures are low.

## Evidence (iMac20,1, kernel 7.2.6-arch2-Watanare-T2-2-t2, t2fanrd r16.48baf96-1)
- After deep-sleep resume: fan1_input ~3608 RPM (min 1200, max 3600), fan1_manual=0, fan1_output=3600, while CPU/GPU sat at ~40C (below the low_temp=55 curve start, so the fan should have been at ~1200).
- fan1_manual/fan1_output mtimes frozen at boot time while all other applesmc attrs were recreated at resume; t2fanrd (PID 902) still running with zero log output after resume.
- sudo systemctl restart t2fanrd flipped manual 0->1 and dropped the fan to ~1199 RPM. Same signature as #12393 (there: under-cooled at high temp; here: over-cooled at low temp).

## Changes
- default/systemd/system-sleep/t2fanrd: new post-resume hook running /usr/bin/systemctl try-restart t2fanrd.service (try-restart so it never starts a deliberately stopped daemon).
- install/hardware/apple/fix-t2.sh: install the hook to /usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/t2fanrd (0755, root-owned) on fresh T2 setups, following the existing hardware-conditional hook pattern (/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep is already an allowed path in unowned-system-paths-test.sh).
- migrations/1789870949.sh: same install for existing T2 installs; no-ops without the T2 PCI ID (106b:180[12]); idempotent.

## Verification
- bash -n passes on all three files; hook source is 0644 like its siblings.
- The equivalent hook was installed manually on the affected iMac and the fan returned to ~1198 RPM with manual=1; the daemon now re-asserts control on every resume instead of needing a manual restart.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,8 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+# t2fanrd holds applesmc fan FDs open across suspend; after resume the sysfs
+# nodes are recreated and the running daemon never reasserts manual control,
+# leaving the SMC in failsafe full speed (fan1_manual=0, ~3600 RPM at 40C).
+# Restart it on resume so fans return to the configured curve in /etc/t2fand.conf.
+# See https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/issues/12393
+[[ $1 == "post" ]] || exit 0
+/usr/bin/systemctl try-restart t2fanrd.service

@@ -47,4 +47,11 @@ high_temp=75
 speed_curve=linear
 always_full_speed=false
 EOF
+
+  # t2fanrd holds applesmc fan FDs open across suspend; after resume it never
+  # reasserts manual control (fan1_manual=0, failsafe full speed).
+  # Restart it on resume so fans return to the configured curve.
+  # See https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/issues/12393
+  sudo install -Dm0755 "$OMARCHY_PATH/default/systemd/system-sleep/t2fanrd" \
+    /usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/t2fanrd
 fi

@@ -0,0 +1,20 @@
+echo "Restore t2fanrd fan control after suspend/resume"
+
+# t2fanrd holds applesmc fan FDs open across suspend; after resume the sysfs
+# nodes are recreated and the running daemon never reasserts manual control,
+# leaving the SMC in failsafe full speed (fan1_manual=0).
+# Fresh installs are covered by install/hardware/apple/fix-t2.sh; this repairs
+# existing T2 machines. See https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/issues/12393
+if ! lspci -nn 2>/dev/null | grep -q "106b:180[12]"; then
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+source="$OMARCHY_PATH/default/systemd/system-sleep/t2fanrd"
+dest=/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/t2fanrd
+if [[ ! -f $source ]]; then
+  echo "Missing $source; rerun omarchy-migrate after updating." >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+sudo mkdir -p "${dest%/*}"
+sudo install -m 0755 -o root -g root -T "$source" "$dest"
